sanskrit: upādhyāyam adhaḥ kṛtvā ṛco 'dhyetu yajūṃṣi ca juhotu ca sa kakṣāgnau bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let him recite the verses of the Ṛc and the Yajus while degrading his own teacher beneath him, and let him offer oblation while consumed in a brushwood fire.

sanskrit: jamadagnir uvāca purīṣam utsṛjatv apsu hantu gāṃ cāpi dohinīm anṛtau maithunaṃ yātu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Jamadagni said: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let him void his excrement into the waters, let him slay even a milch-cow, and let him go to coupling out of season.

sanskrit: dveṣyo bhāryopajīvī syād dūrabandhuś ca vairavān anyonyasyātithiś cāstu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let him be a hateful man living off his wife, his kinsmen estranged, surrounded by enmity, and let such men be guests of one another.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca adhītya vedāṃs tyajatu trīn agnīn apavidhyatu vikrīṇātu tathā somaṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Gautama said: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—having studied the Vedas let him cast them off, let him let his three sacred fires die out, and let him sell the soma.

sanskrit: udapānaplave grāme brāhmaṇo vṛṣalīpatiḥ tasya sālokyatāṃ yātu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let him attain the same world as that brāhmaṇa who, in a village flooded by a broken well, is the husband of a low-caste woman.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca jīvato vai gurūn bhṛtyān bharantv asya pare janāḥ agatir bahuputraḥ syād bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra said: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—while his elders and dependents yet live, let strangers maintain them; let him be destitute though burdened with many sons.

sanskrit: aśucir brahmakūṭo 'stu ṛddhyā caivāpy ahaṃkṛtaḥ karṣako matsarī cāstu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let him be impure, a counterfeit of a brāhmaṇa, made arrogant by his very prosperity, a ploughman, and grudging.

sanskrit: varṣān karotu bhṛtako rājñaś cāstu purohitaḥ ayājyasya bhaved ṛtvig bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let him toil for years as a hireling, let him be a king's house-priest, and let him serve as ritual officiant for a man unfit to sacrifice.

sanskrit: arundhaty uvāca nityaṃ parivadec chvaśrūṃ bhartur bhavatu durmanāḥ ekā svādu samaśnātu bisastainyaṃ karoti yā
english: Arundhatī said: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let her forever revile her mother-in-law, let her be ill-disposed toward her husband, and let her eat the dainty food alone.

sanskrit: jñātīnāṃ gṛhamadhyasthā saktūn attu dinakṣaye abhāgyāvīrasūr astu bisastainyaṃ karoti yā
english: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—dwelling amid the houses of her kin, let her eat parched meal at day's end; let her be luckless and bear no living son.

sanskrit: gaṇḍovāca anṛtaṃ bhāṣatu sadā sādhubhiś ca virudhyatu dadātu kanyāṃ śulkena bisastainyaṃ karoti yā
english: Gaṇḍū said: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let her speak falsehood always, let her quarrel with the good, and let her give her daughter away for a bride-price.

sanskrit: sādhayitvā svayaṃ prāśed dāsye jīvatu caiva ha vikarmaṇā pramīyeta bisastainyaṃ karoti yā
english: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—having cooked the food, let her eat it herself first; let her live in servitude, and let her perish through forbidden deeds.

sanskrit: paśusakha uvāca dāsya eva prajāyeta so 'prasūtir akiṃcanaḥ daivateṣv anamaskāro bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Paśusakha said: Whoever steals the lotus-stalks—let him be born only of a slave-woman, childless and possessing nothing, paying no homage to the gods.

sanskrit: śunaḥsakha uvāca adhvaryave duhitaraṃ dadātu; cchandoge vā caritabrahmacarye ātharvaṇaṃ vedam adhītya vipraḥ; snāyīta yo vai harate bisāni
english: Śunaḥsakha said: Whoever it is that steals the lotus-stalks—let that brāhmaṇa, who has studied the Atharva Veda, give his daughter to an Adhvaryu priest, or to a Chāndoga who has fulfilled his vow of chastity, and then perform his ritual ablution.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ iṣṭam etad dvijātīnāṃ yo 'yaṃ te śapathaḥ kṛtaḥ tvayā kṛtaṃ bisastainyaṃ sarveṣāṃ naḥ śunaḥsakha
english: The seers said: O Śunaḥsakha, this oath you have sworn is the very thing desired by the twice-born; yet it is you who have committed the theft of the lotus-stalks against us all.

sanskrit: śunaḥsakha uvāca nyastam ādyam apaśyadbhir yad uktaṃ kṛtakarmabhiḥ satyam etan na mithyaitad bisastainyaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā
english: Śunaḥsakha said: What was spoken by you, men of accomplished rites who did not see where the stalks were first laid aside—this is true, this is no falsehood: the theft of the lotus-stalks was done by me.

sanskrit: mayā hy antarhitānīha bisānīmāni paśyata parīkṣārthaṃ bhagavatāṃ kṛtam etan mayānaghāḥ rakṣaṇārthaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ bhavatām aham āgataḥ
english: For it was I who hid away these very lotus-stalks—behold them here! O sinless ones, I did this to test you reverend sages, and I have come for the protection of you all.

sanskrit: yātudhānī hy atikruddhā kṛtyaiṣā vo vadhaiṣiṇī vṛṣādarbhiprayuktaiṣā nihatā me tapodhanāḥ
english: O you whose wealth is austerity, this was a fierce demoness, a deadly enchantment seeking your destruction, sent against you by Vṛṣādarbhi—and she has been slain by me.

sanskrit: duṣṭā hiṃsyād iyaṃ pāpā yuṣmān praty agnisaṃbhavā tasmād asmy āgato viprā vāsavaṃ māṃ nibodhata
english: This wicked, sinful thing, born of fire, would have done you harm; therefore I have come, O brāhmaṇas—know me to be Vāsava.

sanskrit: alobhād akṣayā lokāḥ prāptā vaḥ sārvakāmikāḥ uttiṣṭhadhvam itaḥ kṣipraṃ tān avāpnuta vai dvijāḥ
english: By your freedom from greed you have won imperishable worlds where every desire is fulfilled. Rise up from here at once, O twice-born, and attain them.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato maharṣayaḥ prītās tathety uktvā puraṃdaram sahaiva tridaśendreṇa sarve jagmus triviṣṭapam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the great seers, well pleased, said "So be it" to Puraṃdara, and together with Indra, lord of the thirty gods, they all went to heaven.

sanskrit: evam ete mahātmāno bhogair bahuvidhair api kṣudhā paramayā yuktāś chandyamānā mahātmabhiḥ naiva lobhaṃ tadā cakrus tataḥ svargam avāpnuvan
english: Thus these great-souled ones, though oppressed by the keenest hunger and tempted with enjoyments of every kind by exalted beings, gave way to no greed at all, and so they won heaven.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu naro lobhaṃ vivarjayet eṣa dharmaḥ paro rājann alobha iti viśrutaḥ
english: Therefore in all conditions of life a man should renounce greed. This, O king, is the highest dharma, renowned by the name of freedom from greed.

sanskrit: idaṃ naraḥ saccaritaṃ samavāyeṣu kīrtayet sukhabhāgī ca bhavati na ca durgāṇy avāpnute
english: Let a man recite this noble tale in assemblies; he comes to share in happiness and meets with no calamities.

sanskrit: prīyante pitaraś cāsya ṛṣayo devatās tathā yaśodharmārthabhāgī ca bhavati pretya mānavaḥ
english: His ancestors are pleased, and so too the seers and the gods; and after death the man comes to share in glory, dharma, and wealth.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yad vṛttaṃ tīrthayātrāyāṃ śapathaṃ prati tac chṛṇu
english: Bhīṣma said: On this very matter they recount an ancient tale—what came to pass on a pilgrimage to the holy fords, concerning an oath. Hear it.

sanskrit: puṣkarārthaṃ kṛtaṃ stainyaṃ purā bharatasattama rājarṣibhir mahārāja tathaiva ca dvijarṣibhiḥ
english: O best of the Bharatas, in olden days, O great king, a theft was committed over a lotus by royal seers and likewise by brāhmaṇa seers.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ sametāḥ paścime vai prabhāse; samāgatā mantram amantrayanta carāma sarve pṛthivīṃ puṇyatīrthāṃ; tan naḥ kāryaṃ hanta gacchāma sarve
english: The seers, gathered together in the west at Prabhāsa, took counsel among themselves: "Let us all roam the earth and its holy fords—that is our task; come now, let us all set out."

sanskrit: śukro 'ṅgirāś caiva kaviś ca vidvāṃs; tathāgastyo nāradaparvatau ca bhṛgur vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapo gautamaś ca; viśvāmitro jamadagniś ca rājan
english: O king, Śukra and Aṅgiras, and the learned Kavi, and Agastya, and Nārada and Parvata, Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, and Gautama, Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni—

sanskrit: ṛṣis tathā gālavo 'thāṣṭakaś ca; bharadvājo 'rundhatī vālakhilyāḥ śibir dilīpo nahuṣo 'mbarīṣo; rājā yayātir dhundhumāro 'tha pūruḥ
english: and the seer Gālava, and Aṣṭaka, Bharadvāja, Arundhatī, the Vālakhilyas, Śibi, Dilīpa, Nahuṣa, Ambarīṣa, King Yayāti, Dhundhumāra, and Pūru—

sanskrit: jagmuḥ puraskṛtya mahānubhāvaṃ; śatakratuṃ vṛtrahaṇaṃ narendra tīrthāni sarvāṇi parikramanto; māghyāṃ yayuḥ kauśikīṃ puṇyatīrthām
english: O lord of men, setting at their head the mighty Śatakratu, slayer of Vṛtra, they journeyed; circling round all the holy fords, in the month of Māgha they came to the sacred Kauśikī ford.

sanskrit: sarveṣu tīrtheṣv atha dhūtapāpā; jagmus tato brahmasaraḥ supuṇyam devasya tīrthe jalam agnikalpā; vigāhya te bhuktabisaprasūnāḥ
english: Their sins washed away in all the fords, they went then to the most holy Lake of Brahmā; and those sages, splendid as fire, plunging into the water at the god's ford, fed upon lotus-stalks and lotus-blossoms.

sanskrit: ke cid bisāny akhanaṃs tatra rājann; anye mṛṇālāny akhanaṃs tatra viprāḥ athāpaśyan puṣkaraṃ te hriyantaṃ; hradād agastyena samuddhṛtaṃ vai
english: There, O king, some dug up lotus-stalks, and other brāhmaṇas dug up lotus-fibres; then they saw a lotus being carried off, drawn up from the pool by Agastya.

sanskrit: tān āha sarvān ṛṣimukhyān agastyaḥ; kenādattaṃ puṣkaraṃ me sujātam yuṣmāñ śaṅke dīyatāṃ puṣkaraṃ me; na vai bhavanto hartum arhanti padmam
english: Agastya said to all those foremost seers: "By whom was my fair-grown lotus taken? I suspect you. Let my lotus be returned to me—surely you ought not to steal the flower."

sanskrit: śṛṇomi kālo hiṃsate dharmavīryaṃ; seyaṃ prāptā vardhate dharmapīḍā purādharmo vardhate neha yāvat; tāvad gacchāmi paralokaṃ cirāya
english: "I hear that the age destroys the strength of dharma; this oppression of dharma has now come and grows apace. Before unrighteousness here increases further, I shall depart for the other world for a long while."

sanskrit: purā vedān brāhmaṇā grāmamadhye; ghuṣṭasvarā vṛṣalāñ śrāvayanti purā rājā vyavahārān adharmyān; paśyaty ahaṃ paralokaṃ vrajāmi
english: "Before brāhmaṇas, with loud-proclaimed voice, recite the Vedas in the midst of villages for low-caste men to hear, before the king looks on at unrighteous lawsuits, I shall go to the other world."

sanskrit: purāvarān pratyavarān garīyaso; yāvan narā nāvamaṃsyanti sarve tamottaraṃ yāvad idaṃ na vartate; tāvad vrajāmi paralokaṃ cirāya
english: "Before all men come to despise their betters, their elders, and the worthier—while this rule of the worse-over-the-better does not yet prevail—until then I shall depart for the other world for a long while."

sanskrit: purā prapaśyāmi pareṇa martyān; balīyasā durbalān bhujyamānān tasmād yāsyāmi paralokaṃ cirāya; na hy utsahe draṣṭum īdṛṅ nṛloke
english: "Before I see weak mortals devoured by the stronger, by the more powerful—for that reason I shall go to the other world for a long while, for I cannot bear to witness such things in the world of men."

sanskrit: tam āhur ārtā ṛṣayo maharṣiṃ; na te vayaṃ puṣkaraṃ corayāmaḥ mithyābhiṣaṅgo bhavatā na kāryaḥ; śapāma tīkṣṇāñ śapathān maharṣe
english: Distressed, the seers said to that great sage: "We have not stolen your lotus. You ought not to lay a false charge upon us; we shall swear fierce oaths, O great seer."

sanskrit: te niścitās tatra maharṣayas tu; saṃmanyanto dharmam evaṃ narendra tato 'śapañ śapathān paryayeṇa; sahaiva te pārthiva putrapautraiḥ
english: Then those great seers, resolved and reverencing dharma in this manner, O lord of men, swore oaths each in turn, O king, together with their sons and grandsons.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca pratyākrośed ihākruṣṭas tāḍitaḥ pratitāḍayet khādec ca pṛṣṭhamāṃsāni yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Bhṛgu said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him, when reviled, revile back, when struck, strike back, and let him devour the flesh of others' backs through slander.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca asvādhyāyaparo loke śvānaṃ ca parikarṣatu pure ca bhikṣur bhavatu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him be one given over to the neglect of Vedic study, let him drag a dog about, and let him become a beggar in the town.

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca sarvatra sarvaṃ paṇatu nyāse lobhaṃ karotu ca kūṭasākṣitvam abhyetu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Kaśyapa said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him trade in everything everywhere, let him grasp at goods left in his trust, and let him take up the office of false witness.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca jīvatv ahaṃkṛto buddhyā vipaṇatv adhamena saḥ karṣako matsarī cāstu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Gautama said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him live made arrogant by his own cleverness, let him trade in the basest of wares, and let him be a ploughman and grudging.

sanskrit: aṅgirā uvāca aśucir brahmakūṭo 'stu śvānaṃ ca parikarṣatu brahmahānikṛtiś cāstu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Aṅgiras said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him be impure, a counterfeit of a brāhmaṇa, let him drag a dog about, and let him be a destroyer of sacred knowledge.

sanskrit: dhundhumāra uvāca akṛtajño 'stu mitrāṇāṃ śūdrāyāṃ tu prajāyatu ekaḥ saṃpannam aśnātu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Dhundhumāra said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him be ungrateful to his friends, let him beget offspring upon a śūdra woman, and let him eat the finest food alone.

sanskrit: pūrur uvāca cikitsāyāṃ pracaratu bhāryayā caiva puṣyatu śvaśurāt tasya vṛttiḥ syād yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Pūru said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him ply the trade of medicine, let him grow rich through his wife, and let his livelihood come from his father-in-law.

sanskrit: dilīpa uvāca udapānaplave grāme brāhmaṇo vṛṣalīpatiḥ tasya lokān sa vrajatu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Dilīpa said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him go to the worlds of that brāhmaṇa who, in a village flooded by a broken well, is the husband of a low-caste woman.

sanskrit: śukra uvāca pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ samaśnātu divā gacchatu maithunam preṣyo bhavatu rājñaś ca yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Śukra said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him feed on backbiting slander, let him resort to coupling by day, and let him be a king's menial servant.

sanskrit: jamadagnir uvāca anadhyāyeṣv adhīyīta mitraṃ śrāddhe ca bhojayet śrāddhe śūdrasya cāśnīyād yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Jamadagni said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him study on days when study is forbidden, let him feed a mere friend at the funeral rite, and let him eat at a śūdra's funeral feast.

sanskrit: śibir uvāca anāhitāgnir mriyatāṃ yajñe vighnaṃ karotu ca tapasvibhir virudhyeta yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Śibi said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him die without having kindled the sacred fires, let him work obstruction at a sacrifice, and let him quarrel with ascetics.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca anṛtau jaṭī vratinyāṃ vai bhāryāyāṃ saṃprajāyatu nirākarotu vedāṃś ca yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Yayāti said: Whoever steals your lotus—wearing matted locks, let him beget offspring out of season upon a wife bound by a vow, and let him cast aside the Vedas.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca atithiṃ gṛhastho nudatu kāmavṛtto 'stu dīkṣitaḥ vidyāṃ prayacchatu bhṛto yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Nahuṣa said: Whoever steals your lotus—as a householder let him drive away the guest, as a consecrated man let him follow his lusts, and let him sell his learning for hire.

sanskrit: ambarīṣa uvāca nṛśaṃsas tyaktadharmo 'stu strīṣu jñātiṣu goṣu ca brāhmaṇaṃ cāpi jahatu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Ambarīṣa said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him be cruel and forsworn of dharma toward women, kinsmen, and cattle, and let him forsake even the brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca gūḍho 'jñānī bahiḥ śāstraṃ paṭhatāṃ visvaraṃ padam garīyaso 'vajānātu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Nārada said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him be ignorant within while reciting scripture outwardly with discordant, faulty verse, and let him despise his betters.

sanskrit: nābhāga uvāca anṛtaṃ bhāṣatu sadā sadbhiś caiva virudhyatu śulkena kanyāṃ dadatu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Nābhāga said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him speak falsehood always, let him quarrel with the good, and let him give his daughter away for a bride-price.

sanskrit: kavir uvāca padā sa gāṃ tāḍayatu sūryaṃ ca prati mehatu śaraṇāgataṃ ca tyajatu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Kavi said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him kick a cow with his foot, let him make water facing the sun, and let him abandon one who has come to him for refuge.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca karotu bhṛtako 'varṣāṃ rājñaś cāstu purohitaḥ ṛtvig astu hy ayājyasya yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Viśvāmitra said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him toil for years as a hireling, let him be a king's house-priest, and let him serve as ritual officiant for one unfit to sacrifice.

sanskrit: parvata uvāca grāme cādhikṛtaḥ so 'stu kharayānena gacchatu śunaḥ karṣatu vṛttyarthe yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Parvata said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him be set as an officer over a village, let him travel in a donkey-cart, and let him drag dogs about to earn his living.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca sarvapāpasamādānaṃ nṛśaṃse cānṛte ca yat tat tasyāstu sadā pāpaṃ yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Bharadvāja said: Whoever steals your lotus—let there cling to him forever the sin that is the gathering-up of all sins, the sin that lies in cruelty and in falsehood.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca sa rājāstv akṛtaprajñaḥ kāmavṛttiś ca pāpakṛt adharmeṇānuśāstūrvīṃ yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Aṣṭaka said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him be a king devoid of wisdom, a lustful evildoer, and let him rule the earth by unrighteousness.

sanskrit: gālava uvāca pāpiṣṭhebhyas tv anarghārhaḥ sa naro 'stu svapāpakṛt dattvā dānaṃ kīrtayatu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Gālava said: Whoever steals your lotus—let that man be worth less than the vilest of the wicked, a worker of his own sin, and let him boast aloud of the gift he has given.

sanskrit: arundhaty uvāca śvaśrvāpavādaṃ vadatu bhartur bhavatu durmanāḥ ekā svādu samaśnātu yā te harati puṣkaram
english: Arundhatī said: Whoever steals your lotus—let her speak ill of her mother-in-law, let her be ill-disposed toward her husband, and let her eat the dainty food alone.

sanskrit: vālakhilyā ūcuḥ ekapādena vṛttyarthaṃ grāmadvāre sa tiṣṭhatu dharmajñas tyaktadharmo 'stu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: The Vālakhilyas said: Whoever steals your lotus—let him stand on one foot at the village gate to earn his bread, and though he knows dharma, let him be forsworn of dharma.

sanskrit: paśusakha uvāca agnihotram anādṛtya sukhaṃ svapatu sa dvijaḥ parivrāṭ kāmavṛtto 'stu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Paśusakha said: Whoever steals your lotus—let that twice-born man sleep at ease, neglecting the fire-oblation, and as a wandering renunciant let him follow his lusts.

sanskrit: surabhy uvāca bālvajena nidānena kāṃsyaṃ bhavatu dohanam duhyeta paravatsena yā te harati puṣkaram
english: Surabhi said: Whoever steals your lotus—let her tether the cow with a halter of coarse grass, let her milking-pail be of bronze, and let her milk with another's calf at the udder.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas tu taiḥ śapathaiḥ śapyamānair; nānāvidhair bahubhiḥ kauravendra sahasrākṣo devarāṭ saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ; samīkṣya taṃ kopanaṃ vipramukhyam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, O lord of the Kurus, as they swore those many and various oaths, the thousand-eyed sovereign of the gods rejoiced greatly, gazing upon that wrathful chief of brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: athābravīn maghavā pratyayaṃ svaṃ; samābhāṣya tam ṛṣiṃ jātaroṣam brahmarṣidevarṣinṛparṣimadhye; yat tan nibodheha mamādya rājan
english: Then Maghavat, addressing that seer who had grown enraged, declared his own avowal in the midst of the brāhmaṇa-seers, the divine seers, and the royal seers—mark now, O king, what I tell you here today.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca adhvaryave duhitaraṃ dadātu; cchandoge vā caritabrahmacarye ātharvaṇaṃ vedam adhītya vipraḥ; snāyīta yaḥ puṣkaram ādadāti
english: Śakra said: Whoever it is that takes your lotus—let that brāhmaṇa, having studied the Atharva Veda, give his daughter to an Adhvaryu priest, or to a Chāndoga who has fulfilled his vow of chastity, and then perform his ablution.

sanskrit: sarvān vedān adhīyīta puṇyaśīlo 'stu dhārmikaḥ brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ yātu yas te harati puṣkaram
english: Whoever steals your lotus—let him study all the Vedas, let him be of holy character and righteous, and let him go to the abode of Brahmā.

sanskrit: agastya uvāca āśīrvādas tvayā proktaḥ śapatho balasūdana dīyatāṃ puṣkaraṃ mahyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Agastya said: What you have uttered, O slayer of Bala, is a blessing, not an oath of cursing. Let my lotus be returned to me—that is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: indra uvāca na mayā bhagavaṃl lobhād dhṛtaṃ puṣkaram adya vai dharmaṃ tu śrotukāmena hṛtaṃ na kroddhum arhasi
english: Indra said: Reverend one, I did not take this lotus today out of greed; I took it from a wish to hear an exposition of dharma. You ought not to be angry.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ śrutisamutkarṣo dharmasetur anāmayaḥ ārṣo vai śāśvato nityam avyayo 'yaṃ mayā śrutaḥ
english: This dharma I have now heard—the exaltation of sacred lore, the flawless dike of righteousness—belonging to the seers, everlasting, eternal, and imperishable.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ gṛhyatāṃ vidvan puṣkaraṃ munisattama atikramaṃ me bhagavan kṣantum arhasy anindita
english: So take back this lotus, O learned one, O best of sages; reverend and blameless one, you ought to forgive my transgression.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa mahendreṇa tapasvī kopano bhṛśam jagrāha puṣkaraṃ dhīmān prasannaś cābhavan muniḥ
english: Thus addressed by great Indra, that ascetic, sorely wrathful though he was, took back the lotus; and the wise sage became serene.

sanskrit: prayayus te tato bhūyas tīrthāni vanagocarāḥ puṇyatīrtheṣu ca tathā gātrāṇy āplāvayanti te
english: Then those forest-dwelling sages went on once more to the holy fords, and at the sacred fords they bathed their limbs.

sanskrit: ākhyānaṃ ya idaṃ yuktaḥ paṭhet parvaṇi parvaṇi na mūrkhaṃ janayet putraṃ na bhavec ca nirākṛtiḥ
english: Whoever, devout, reads this tale at every change of the moon will beget no foolish son, nor will he himself be cast out.

sanskrit: na tam āpat spṛśet kā cin na jvaro na rujaś ca ha virajāḥ śreyasā yuktaḥ pretya svargam avāpnuyāt
english: No calamity will touch him, nor fever, nor disease; freed of impurity and endowed with blessedness, after death he will attain heaven.

sanskrit: yaś ca śāstram anudhyāyed ṛṣibhiḥ paripālitam sa gacched brahmaṇo lokam avyayaṃ ca narottama
english: And whoever meditates upon this scripture, guarded by the seers, will go, O best of men, to the imperishable world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ śrāddhadharmeṣu dīyate bharatarṣabha chatraṃ copānahau caiva kenaitat saṃpravartitam kathaṃ caitat samutpannaṃ kimarthaṃ ca pradīyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O bull of the Bharatas, the umbrella and the pair of sandals that are given away in the rites of the funeral offering—by whom was this first set in motion? How did it come to be, and for what purpose is it given?
